audit_2026_11_10: FRESH AUDIT PASSED (first-hand, 2026-11-10) — post-WAVE1 order worked in the 2026-11-10 candidate audits: Jacksonville FL, Gwinnett GA, Cobb GA, DuPage IL, San Jose CA, Rochester NY, El Paso TX, Dayton OH, Akron OH, and Syracuse NY surfaced no engine-ready record-level permit feed (SKIP); Greensboro NC's layer was not verifiable in-session (connection closed, verdict unverified); Cleveland OH passed. (1) Layer 'Building_Permits' (City of Cleveland 'Issued Building Permits' FeatureServer, ArcGIS item owner opendataCLE, public access): 202,884 rows all-time, every row carries ISSUE_DATE (permits issued 2015 to present, per the item description, by the Department of Building and Housing); item states Update Frequency 'Weekly on Sundays'; layer editingInfo.dataLastEditDate 2026-11-08T12:18:35Z (a Sunday). (2) VOLUME STABILITY measured by issued year (single-bound ladder): 2020 14,590 / 2021 15,561 / 2022 15,660 / 2023 15,436 / 2024 15,905 / 2025 16,315 / 2026 YTD 12,425 — no collapse; window months run 683-1,442. (3) IDENTITY measured three ways on the window (two count queries + one full paged pull saved as the audit evidence): 14,455 rows = 14,455 distinct PERMIT_ID = 14,455 distinct OBJECTID, 0 duplicates, 0 null ids — one row per permit, no collapsing. September 2026 cross-check figure: 1,311 permits; October 2026: 1,333; November 2026 to Nov 7: 325; latest issue date 2026-11-07. (4) VALUATION PASSED — values publish (see field_map.valuation). (5) Terms: the item's licenseInfo states the Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL); figures are published 'as reported by the City of Cleveland' with attribution. Audit evidence: ~/workspace/goals/permitsbycounty/hidden_files/expansion-2026-11-10/.
coverage_note: Permits issued by the City of Cleveland only. Other Cuyahoga County jurisdictions publish their permits separately and are not in this feed; totals here are City of Cleveland totals, labeled as such.

dedupe_rule.definition: One published permit = one PERMIT_ID in the City of Cleveland's Issued Building Permits layer. The layer's grain is one row per permit: no collapsing applies or is needed.
dedupe_rule.measurement: Trailing-12-month window (ISSUE_DATE >= 2025-11-10), measured 2026-11-10 on three consistent reads (two count queries + a full paged pull of the window): 14,455 rows = 14,455 distinct PERMIT_ID = 14,455 distinct OBJECTID, 0 duplicates, 0 null permit numbers. The pipeline's in-batch duplicate gate and the (county_id, source_record_id) upsert key guard every future pull.

field_map.address: PRIMARY_ADDRESS, as published (present on 14,449 of 14,455 window permits): the full string carries street, city, state, and ZIP ('8501 CARNEGIE AVE, CLEVELAND, OH, 44106'); the street portion is carried as the address (title-cased, the Columbus treatment), the city is Cleveland, and the ZIP is parsed from the string's trailing ZIP or ZIP+4 (34 window addresses state no ZIP or a ZIP+4 variant and are parsed by the same rule).
field_map.application_date: FILE_DATE (epoch ms in the ArcGIS feed, converted to the civil date; present on 100% of window permits).
field_map.category: The source's own residential/commercial naming: PERMIT_CATEGORY values that name a class ('Residential Building', 'Residential Electrical', ...) and, for the categories that state no class ('Board-ups', 'New', 'Electrical', 'Plumbing', 'HVAC and Refrigeration'), the PERMIT_SUBTYPE class ('Residential' / 'Commercial'). Window: Residential 10,744 / Commercial 3,461 / unstated 250 (the elevator, escalator, and fire-suppression families, whose records state no class).
field_map.contractor_rule: CONTRATOR_BUSINESS_NAME ONLY (the source's own field spelling, missing the second C) — the permit's published contractor BUSINESS name of record (present on 12,909 of 14,455 window permits; 1,911 distinct; empty string carries as NULL). The pull's column list never requests CONTRACTOR_NAME (the installer of record — a PERSON name, present on 12,911 rows) or CONTRATOR_LICENSE_ID — both excluded from pull_select by construction.
field_map.issue_date: ISSUE_DATE (epoch ms in the ArcGIS feed, converted to the civil date). The window is defined on it: a record enters this report when the city records an issue date; every row in the layer carries one (the dataset is the city's issued-permits register).
field_map.permit_number: PERMIT_ID (unique in the window, see dedupe_rule).
field_map.permit_type: PERMIT_CATEGORY, the city's own permit family (Residential Building, Commercial Electrical, Board-ups, New, Elevator Dumbwaiter, ...).
field_map.project_description: WORK_DESCRIPTION, the source's own free-text scope of work (present on 14,453 of 14,455 window permits); JOB_DESCRIPTION (the city's shorter work class, present on 7,327) is the fallback where the scope text is empty. No description is invented.
field_map.status: CURRENT_TASK_STATUS, mapped through status_map; the verbatim source value is kept in status_source. The layer is an issued-permits register, so its workflow states are all post-issuance states (Permit Closed 7,331 / Inspection Pending 5,969 / Permit Issuance Approved 613 / the certificate, inspection-approved, and closure families / Closed - Discard and Discard, which map to withdrawn). One source value is misspelled in the feed itself ('nspection Pending', 1 window permit) and is mapped alongside its correct spelling.
field_map.valuation: JOB_VALUE PUBLISHES, as reported: present on 100% of the 14,455 window permits — $0 on 1,673 (1,133 of them board-up permits, which state $0 by construction), $1 on only 67, negative on 0, above $1 on 12,715; DB trailing-12-month sum must reproduce the independently computed $1,719,595,874.40. Validation measured 2026-11-10 on the full window: the largest permit ($101,000,000, a new building at 8501 Carnegie Ave) appears exactly once and is 5.9% of the total — a flagship, not a stamp; repeated values at $1M or more are round applicant budgets ($1,000,000 on 12 permits at distinct addresses — the Cincinnati/Boston signature), not a non-round system stamp (contrast Seattle); same-address + same-value groups above $10k bound any sibling-permit restatement excess at $25,797,100.45, 1.50% of the total; and every trade family states per-permit values (electrical medians $3,200-$13,000, plumbing $3,000-$20,000, HVAC $5,795-$20,500), so the Columbus fee-basis-absence defect does not exist here. The $45,081,467 'Fence' permit at 5300 Riverside Dr is a 51,000-linear-foot airport perimeter security fence per its own work description — a plausible per-permit scope, carried as reported (SOP rule 2).

history_range: ISSUE_DATE 2015 onward in the source (202,884 rows, per the item description 'permits issued from 2015 to present'); we backfill the trailing 12 months only (site rule).
license: Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL), named in the ArcGIS item's licenseInfo; attribution: City of Cleveland, Ohio
rate_limit: ArcGIS hosted FeatureServer query, 1,000-row pages (the layer's maxRecordCount) with the adapter's 0.4s pacing plus retries; anonymous public tier served the full audit and backfill pulls steadily.
source_name: City of Cleveland open data — Issued Building Permits
terms_status: verified-open-2026-11-10: the ArcGIS item record for 'Issued Building Permits' (publisher: City of Cleveland, Department of Building and Housing, owner opendataCLE; access public) states the Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL) in its licenseInfo; figures are published 'as reported by the City of Cleveland' with attribution; no endorsement is implied.
update_cadence: Weekly on Sundays (the item's own stated update frequency; the city reloads the dataset in a weekly batch). MEASURED 2026-11-10: layer dataLastEditDate 2026-11-08T12:18:35Z (a Sunday, ~62h old at the audit) and newest ISSUE_DATE 2026-11-07. Freshness (gate 5) is measured as the layer's editingInfo.dataLastEditDate under a 240h threshold sized to the stated weekly cadence (the Los Angeles treatment).
watermark_field: ISSUE_DATE + PERMIT_ID — refresh re-pulls by the ISSUE_DATE watermark and upserts.
